title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash API: Pricing, Specs & Features (2026)
summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash API integration requires specific authentication steps to manage your usage costs.
body_markdown:
## Understand DeepSeek V4.1 Flash pricing tiers


DeepSeek V4.1 Flash uses a tiered pricing model that heavily discounts repetitive context to lower the overhead of long-running agentic loops.


This architecture, described by[DeepSeek](https://deepseek.com/en/news/deepseek-v4-1-flash) as the smallest model in their new family with native visual understanding, allows for aggressive price compression when you structure prompts to hit the cache.


### Input and output token costs as of September 2026


By pricing output tokens at four times the rate of uncached input tokens, the cost structure for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash prioritizes high-volume throughput. The following figures represent the cost per 1 million tokens in USD:


- Cached Input: $0.003
- Uncached Input: $0.15
- Output: $0.60


**If a developer fails to optimize for caching, they pay 50 times more for input than one who does.**


### Visual token calculation and pricing


Visual inputs are billed based on a fixed token count per image rather than a variable resolution scale. Each image uploaded to the V4.1 Flash endpoint consumes exactly 1,600 tokens, which are billed at the standard uncached input rate of $0.15 per million tokens.


> **If a developer fails to optimize for caching, they pay 50 times more for input than one who does.


This results in a flat cost of $0.00024 per image, making visual understanding highly predictable for high-speed automated workflows.


### DeepSeek V4.1 Flash context caching discount


The **98% discount on cached inputs** makes DeepSeek V4.1 Flash a viable option for RAG systems where the same documentation is prepended to every query. According to the[DeepSeek API documentation](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news260910) , this caching mechanism triggers automatically on identical prefixes.


### How DeepSeek prefix cache matching works


Caching is handled server-side through exact string matching of the prompt prefix. To trigger the discount, the identical prefix must be at least 1024 tokens long and aligned to 64-token blocks.


Developers should structure prompts by placing static content like system instructions and reference documents at the very beginning of the message array.


By keeping the variable user query at the end of the prompt, the system can reuse the cached state of the preceding tokens. If you change a single character at the start of the prompt, the entire cache for that request is invalidated.


This behavior makes it critical to maintain a consistent order for all shared context across multiple API calls.


### Rate limits for Free, Pay-as-you-go, and Enterprise tiers


To prevent small-scale testing from disrupting production traffic, DeepSeek segments its API capacity into three tiers. The Free Tier provides a low requests-per-minute (RPM) ceiling, suitable only for initial integration tests.


Based on total account spend, the Pay-as-you-go Tier increases the RPM and tokens-per-minute (TPM) limits. The Enterprise Tier grants dedicated throughput and the highest rate limits to avoid the 429 Too Many Requests errors that plague shared public pools.
